title: The story that launched bystander-effect research was badly exaggerated
body: In 1964 The New York Times reported that 37 witnesses saw or heard Kitty Genovese being attacked in New York and none called police or helped. Later investigations found far fewer people saw anything, many didn’t realise how serious it was, and some did try to call police; in 2016 the Times itself called its reporting flawed. The story still inspired valuable research on bystanders, though studies of real conflicts caught on camera find that someone usually steps in.

slides.question: What do studies of real conflicts caught on camera tend to find?
slides.explanation: Despite the famous story, studies of real conflicts caught on camera find that someone usually steps in to help.
